notes: Seeded and written by the same model family that runs the fallback passes; read the scores as a comparison between arms on the same key, not as an absolute measure. Each item and decoy has a proof in bench/proofs/ (items fail at sha, decoys pass). pass_at (7 of 10, about two thirds) and max_decoy_hits are a first, arbitrary bar. R4 was not planted: the first fallback run found it and it was added with its proof. Known real issue left out of the key: Exports.total_size (files.py 31-32) lists then stats, so a concurrent remove_export makes it raise; it sits within 15 lines of D6, so it cannot be an item until the next sha bump moves one of them. A run that reports it is right, and the score ignores it.

items.title: Pagination drops the last order of every page
Mutable default list leaks the sale label into later products
to_cents promises half-up rounding but rounds half to even on a float
Two buyers can reserve the last unit: check and update are not atomic
A charge retried after a timeout has no idempotency key and can charge twice
The worker acknowledges a message before handling it, so a failure loses it
Rewriting an export truncates it in place, so a reader in between sees it empty or partial
Search text is interpolated into SQL
Any signed-in user can read any order
Export names can leave the exports folder

decoys.title: ORDER BY column comes from a fixed map, values are parameters
Order numbering is under the lock
Retrying a status read is safe: it is a GET
random only adds jitter to retry delays
The worker logs the send error and raises it again
Report names are resolved and checked against the reports folder
